To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cholinesterase is present at the myoneu- ral junction in human inter-costal muscle and that the activity is demonstrable histochemically for at least 157 days after death in refrigerated muscle and for a similar period in muscle removed from bodies within a day of embalming.

cholinesterase is present in the myoneural region of human intercostal and other skeletal muscle, and that the enzyme activity can be demonstrated histochemically up to 157 d postmortem in muscle that is refrigerated and in muscle removed from bodies within the first day after embalming, and that the activity can also be demonstrated in muscle fixed in various fixatives.
Cholinesterase is a hydrolase enzyme which catalyses the hydrolysis of choline esters to choline and a carboxylic acid (e. g., acetic acid in the case of acetylcholine).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the histochemical demonstration of cholinesterases in post-mortem tissues.
the histochemical localization of acetylcholine esterase in the myoneural synapses in human skeletal muscle.
the study of the effects of the cholinesterase inhibitors and the cholinesterases inhibitors and the choline esters on the cholinergic transmission in the autonomic ganglion.

choline-sterase activity is present in human post-mortem tissue for at least 157 days.
the duration of cholinesterease activity in muscle tissue, whether refrigerated or embalmed, is not a reliable criterion in determining the time since death.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the activity of this enzyme may be demonstrated in human muscle for long periods after death, it is not a useful indicator for the time of death in this species.
cholinesterase is a very resistant enzyme and that it is unlikely to disappear from muscle in the course of post-mortem changes.
cholinesterase can be demonstrated in post-mortem tissue for a considerable period of time and that the enzyme is resistant to the action of many fixatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now measure cholinesterase in the post-mortem period.
the duration of post-mortem cholinesterase in muscle is longer than previously reported and that the activity can be preserved by certain fixatives.
the cholinesterase reaction is not specific for acetylcholine, and it is not clear whether the enzyme is involved in acetylcholine hydrolysis at all.
